scenarios.name: invoice-with-pdf-and-tags
scenarios.rationale: Both meet the core rubric (attachments with filename and a file Buffer, tags as name/value objects, destructured { data, error } with an error check, camelCase), but A is labeled typescript while using .mjs-style ESM and its notes say 'Idempotency-Key header' without showing it. B's error handling is cleaner (console.error plus exit), and it reads the file before the call, includes a run command and gives the tag character constraints.

scenarios.name: verified-webhook-for-bounces
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it reads the body with req.text(), verifies with resend.webhooks.verify using the svix-id, svix-timestamp and svix-signature headers and a webhookSecret from an env var, handles both events, returns 400 on a failed verification, and tests through ngrok with bounced@resend.dev; A reads the raw body and handles both events but verifies with the svix library instead of resend.webhooks.verify, returns 401 instead of 400 on a bad signature, and treats only permanent bounces as undeliverable, though it does cover the tunnel and bounced@resend.dev.

scenarios.name: batch-weekly-digest-react-email
scenarios.rationale: A uses resend.batch.send with mapped payloads, chunks of 100, calls DigestEmail({ items }) as a function, mentions no attachments/scheduledAt and the 'react-email' import; B uses JSX in react, imports from '@react-email/components', and doesn't call the template as a function, though it does chunk and map correctly.
